answer: To raise the cost of mass clones, each newcomer must forge an identity by locking stake that only unlocks after several epochs of independent peer grading. That escrow behaves like a river: splitting one agent into many identities shallows every copy below the admission depth. A falcon audit then samples pairwise work traces and nonce patterns, slashing the bond when clusters share a model or replayed output, so fake majorities cannot harvest settlement rewards.
